atlas-ie.0067: Careers services across 26 universities, technological universities and institutes belong to AHECS, which works with gradireland and runs the Early Careers Employers Survey.
atlas-ie.0068: A foreign qualification gets a non-binding comparability statement from NARIC Ireland (QQI); formal recognition decisions are made by institutions, professional bodies and employers.
atlas-ie.0069: Gradireland Graduate Careers Fair, RDS Dublin, 6 October 2026, 11:00 to 17:00, open to students and graduates, with over 80 employers and talks on CVs, interviews and working in Ireland as an international student.
atlas-ie.0070: Trinity College Dublin Engineering and Environment Fair and UCC Recruitment Festival on 8 October; ATU Galway Careers Fair on 20 October; University of Limerick spring fair on 27 and 28 January and 10 and 11 February.
atlas-ie.0071: Firm deadlines: Deloitte’s 2027 Future Leaders Academy closes on 21 October 2026, and PwC’s summer internship opens on 2 December 2026 and closes on 29 January 2027.
atlas-ie.0072: Dublin’s funds industry hires graduates into fund accounting, administration and depositary roles: State Street, the largest fund administrator in Ireland, runs a 12-month in-person internship, and administrators backed a new master’s in investment fund administration with two Irish universities.
atlas-ie.0073: Bank of Ireland says its 2027 Graduate Programme is closed and invites registration of interest in the 2028 programme.
atlas-ie.0074: The Big Four and Accenture are named the top employers for Irish graduates; PwC Ireland’s annual drive has been reported at about 250 to 280 graduates, most into training contracts in Dublin.
atlas-ie.0075: KPMG Ireland’s ACA route runs the Chartered Accountant qualification alongside client work; EY applications go through an online form, an online assessment and two interviews.
atlas-ie.0076: Consulting graduates come through the Big Four and Accenture programmes: KPMG Ireland hires into Consulting and Deal Advisory teams, and Deloitte’s Future Leaders Academy welcomes commerce, science and engineering backgrounds.
atlas-ie.0077: The public service recruits through publicjobs.ie, which lists civil-service graduate opportunities, state boards and Garda trainees; the page does not state nationality or right-to-work conditions.
atlas-ie.0078: Graduate software roles come from multinationals and their Irish sites, such as Mastercard’s launch programme in Dublin and Stryker’s R&D graduate programme in Cork; employers keep hiring full-stack, mobile and embedded engineers, with Python, JavaScript and C/C++ most in demand.
atlas-ie.0079: Information and communication had a vacancy rate of 1.6% in the last quarter of 2025, and a software development apprenticeship of two years at NFQ level 6 exists alongside the degree route.
atlas-ie.0080: Data and AI teams at Google, Meta, Microsoft and the payment firms in Dublin hire mainly experienced staff; graduates enter through analyst and operations roles first.
atlas-ie.0081: Gradireland says the majority of companies in Ireland have no specific deadline and accept applications for most or all of the year; the professional-services firms are the exception, with fixed closing dates such as Deloitte’s 21 October 2026.
atlas-ie.0082: The routes read ask for a bachelor’s degree with a 2.1 or 2:1 in any discipline (Deloitte, EY) and name no master’s requirement; a master’s matters for fund administration and some technical roles.
atlas-ie.0083: NARIC Ireland, hosted by QQI, gives free non-binding comparability statements for foreign qualifications, covering over 1,800 qualifications from 170 countries; recognition for a regulated profession is decided by the professional body.
atlas-ie.0084: The selection criteria employers report are competencies (65%) and a 2:1 or better (54%), and the Big Four pages accept any discipline without naming schools.
atlas-ie.0085: Paid placements are built into many Irish degrees, and apprenticeships have grown to 87 programmes with 30,536 apprentices, including degree-level routes in insurance.
atlas-ie.0086: The public service recruits through publicjobs.ie and runs civil-service graduate and ICT apprenticeship routes, but the large graduate intakes read are in the Big Four, banks and multinationals.
atlas-ie.0087: A Critical Skills Employment Permit needs an offer of at least €40,904 (€36,848 for a degree under 12 months old) for two years, no labour-market test, and an employer with at least 50% EEA staff; Deloitte’s programme asks for the legal right to work in Ireland. See Visas for the rules.
atlas-ie.0088: Irish CVs follow British practice: no photo, two pages.
atlas-ie.0089: Careers-service guidance says including a photograph is not the convention in Ireland.
atlas-ie.0090: An Irish CV is two A4 pages with a personal profile, in reverse chronological order; leave off date of birth, PPS number, marital status and nationality.
atlas-ie.0091: Gradireland says a cover letter is needed when a role asks for a traditional CV, but most graduate employers now use online application forms.
atlas-ie.0092: Named referees are common in Ireland and the UK, provided they have agreed to be listed; otherwise a line saying references are available on request is used.
atlas-ie.0093: The application routes read (KPMG, Deloitte, EY) ask for an online form and CV; none asks for transcripts or certified copies at the first stage.
atlas-ie.0094: The online applications read do not ask for a salary expectation; pay is discussed at the offer stage. Critical Skills thresholds count basic salary and qualifying health insurance but not bonuses.
atlas-ie.0095: No page read describes routine background or reference checks; right-to-work is checked, since Deloitte requires the legal right to work in the Republic of Ireland.
atlas-ie.0096: Online applications to graduate programmes are the main channel.
atlas-ie.0097: Gradireland’s survey found the first screening is usually a telephone interview (46%) or online tests (42% ability, 39% psychometric), not a personal introduction.
atlas-ie.0098: EU citizens can apply from anywhere; non-EU graduates of Irish universities can stay one or two years to work.
atlas-ie.0099: Stamp 1G gives non-EEA graduates of Irish awards 12 months at Level 8 or 24 months at Level 9 and above, with full-time work for any employer.
atlas-ie.0100: English; other European languages are in demand in multinationals’ operations.
atlas-ie.0101: Only 2.4 to 2.8% of Irish job postings say English is not required.
atlas-ie.0102: Typical graduate selection: an online application, then online tests or a telephone interview, then interviews. EY runs an online form and CV, an online assessment (scenario ranking, sliders and written answers), an interview with a team and a final strengths-based interview with leadership, in person or on MS Teams.
atlas-ie.0103: Gradireland’s employer survey: 46% use a telephone interview, 42% online ability or technical tests, 39% online psychometric tests and 37% video interviews. EY’s case-study interview for Financial Services Consulting lasts 90 minutes and the competency interview 45 minutes.
atlas-ie.0104: Interviews are in English. The pages read give no typical time from application to offer, nor assessment-centre norms beyond the stages above.
atlas-ie.0105: Since 16 December 2022 a probation period is generally limited to six months, extendable to a maximum of 12 months only in exceptional cases in the employee’s interest; it must be stated in the written terms of employment.
atlas-ie.0106: After 13 weeks’ service statutory notice from the employer starts at one week and rises to eight weeks after 15 years, and the employee owes one week unless the contract says more.
atlas-ie.0107: The ACA route at KPMG Ireland combines the Chartered Accountant qualification with client work; the pages read do not state salaries, bonuses or how long you have to accept an offer.
atlas-ie.0108: The Critical Skills Employment Permit needs a job offer of at least two years paying €40,904 a year (€36,848 if the degree is under 12 months old) or more than €68,911 in any eligible occupation; the employer must apply at least 12 weeks before the start, pay a €1,000 fee (90% refunded if refused) and have at least 50% EEA employees.
atlas-ie.0109: Graduates of Irish awards who hold Stamp 2 can work full time for any employer on Stamp 1G for 12 months (Level 8) or 24 months (Level 9 and above), so an employer need not sponsor you at first; Deloitte still asks for the legal right to work in Ireland.
atlas-ie.0110: Ask early: a Critical Skills application must reach the Department at least 12 weeks before the start date, so an employer needs notice well before the offer is signed.
atlas-ie.0111: Graduate content: gradireland (graduate jobs, programmes, internships, employer A-Z, events, CV and interview guides); employers’ own pages (KPMG, Deloitte, EY, PwC, Bank of Ireland).
atlas-ie.0112: University careers services: 26 institutions in AHECS, which lists fairs such as UCC Recruitment Festival, the Trinity engineering fair and the University of Limerick autumn and spring fairs.
atlas-ie.0113: Public service: publicjobs.ie, with search, alerts and application, test and interview advice.
atlas-ie.0114: Fairs: the Gradireland Graduate Careers Fair at the RDS Dublin (6 October 2026, over 80 employers), held every autumn, open to graduates and students.
atlas-ie.0115: Waiting for a UK-style December deadline: most firms take applications all year, but Deloitte closed on 21 October 2026 and EY closes once its roles are filled.
atlas-ie.0116: Applying to many programmes at one firm: Deloitte lets you apply to only one graduate programme, and EY lets you name two preferences.
atlas-ie.0117: Copying a generic CV template: gradireland warns against it, and the CV should be two pages without photo, date of birth or PPS number.
atlas-ie.0118: Ignoring the degree grade: 54% of graduate employers look for a 2:1 or better, and Deloitte and EY both set a 2.1 or 2:1 as the minimum.
atlas-ie.0119: Not mentioning Stamp 1G: after an Irish degree it allows 12 or 24 months of work for any employer, so a non-EU graduate does not need a sponsor at the start.
